dataHandling: The selected image is processed in your browser. Anvil Tools does not upload it to a conversion server; the page loads the removal model and code needed to perform the local calculation.
limitations: Automatic segmentation can miss hair, glass, shadows, fine edges, or low-contrast subjects. Large images can use significant device memory, and the result should be inspected before reuse.
sensitiveData: Better than upload-based tools, but review the output and device policy.
notes: A model is loaded in the browser; no Anvil conversion upload.

dataHandling: Text is encoded or decoded in your browser and is not sent to an Anvil processing server.
limitations: Base64 is an encoding, not encryption. This tool is for text, and malformed input, variant alphabets, or binary file workflows may require a dedicated decoder.
sensitiveData: Suitable for local text, subject to your device and browser security.
notes: Text-only workflow; encoded text remains readable after decoding.

dataHandling: Palette generation and color locking happen in your browser. No palette values are uploaded to an Anvil processing server.
limitations: Generated colors are starting points, not an accessibility guarantee. Check contrast, color-vision needs, print behavior, and brand requirements separately.
sensitiveData: Suitable; the tool processes only color values locally.
notes: Run a separate contrast check before using text/background pairs.

dataHandling: CSV text is parsed in your browser and is not uploaded to an Anvil processing server.
limitations: The parser targets common comma-delimited CSV. Delimiter variants, inconsistent row widths, spreadsheet formulas, encodings, and very large datasets need separate checks.
sensitiveData: Suitable for local text, but remove confidential data when a synthetic sample will do.
notes: Values remain strings; validate the receiving schema separately.

dataHandling: The browser calculates the digest from UTF-8 text. The input and hash are not sent to an Anvil processing server.
limitations: A hash does not encrypt data, prove authorship, or safely store passwords by itself. Unicode normalization and byte-for-byte input differences produce different results.
sensitiveData: Suitable for local text, but hashes can still reveal information about weak inputs.
notes: Text input only; use a dedicated file hash utility for files.

dataHandling: Selected images are assembled into a PDF in your browser and are not sent to an Anvil conversion server.
limitations: The PDF contains image pages rather than OCR text. Page size follows image dimensions, and large batches can exceed browser memory or create large downloads.
sensitiveData: Suitable for local files, subject to your device and browser security.
notes: Review page order, dimensions, and readability before sharing.

lab.title: JPEG, PNG, and WebP conversion report

dataHandling: JSON is parsed and formatted in your browser and is not sent to an Anvil processing server.
limitations: Parsing does not validate an API schema. Duplicate object keys collapse, unsafe numeric integers can lose precision, and very large documents may strain browser memory.
sensitiveData: Suitable for local text, but use synthetic data whenever possible.
notes: Successful formatting proves syntax, not semantic correctness.

dataHandling: The token header and payload are decoded in your browser. The token is not uploaded to an Anvil processing server.
limitations: Decoding does not verify a signature, issuer, audience, expiry policy, or trust. A readable token can still be forged or invalid.
sensitiveData: Avoid real bearer tokens; use a synthetic or redacted token.
notes: Inspection is not authentication or signature verification.

dataHandling: Passwords are generated in your browser and are not sent to or stored by an Anvil processing server.
limitations: The tool is not a password manager, breach checker, or recovery service. Destination sites may reject particular lengths or symbols, and generated values disappear when you leave.
sensitiveData: Suitable for local generation; save the result directly in a trusted password manager.
notes: Use a unique password per account and enable MFA where available.

dataHandling: Selected PDFs are combined in your browser and are not sent to an Anvil merge server.
limitations: Encrypted files and complex signatures, forms, bookmarks, attachments, tags, and accessibility structures may not be preserved. Large documents can exceed device memory.
sensitiveData: Suitable for local files, subject to your device and browser security.
notes: Inspect the merged file before relying on forms, signatures, or accessibility.

dataHandling: The QR symbol is generated in your browser. The payload is not sent to an Anvil processing server.
limitations: Scan reliability depends on payload length, size, contrast, quiet zone, printing, camera, damage, and environment. Always test the final artifact and destination.
sensitiveData: Suitable for local generation, but anyone who scans the code can read its payload.
notes: The current UI uses a fixed high error-correction setting.

dataHandling: Temporary addresses and messages pass through the Anvil backend and the Guerrilla Mail service so mail can be received. Do not use the inbox for sensitive, recovery, financial, medical, or private messages.
limitations: Delivery, sender acceptance, availability, retention, and deletion are not guaranteed. Some services block disposable addresses, and website access expiry is not proof of provider-side deletion.
externalService: Guerrilla Mail through the Anvil backend
sensitiveData: No. Use only non-sensitive test messages.
notes: The tool interface and every inbox, message, loading, error, and generated-address state are ad-free.

dataHandling: Text transformations happen in your browser and are not sent to an Anvil processing server.
limitations: Automatic case conversion is not language-aware editing. Acronyms, proper names, punctuation, locale-specific casing, and identifier conventions may need manual correction.
sensitiveData: Suitable for local text, subject to your device and browser security.
notes: Review names, acronyms, and code identifiers after conversion.

dataHandling: Both text versions are compared in your browser and are not sent to an Anvil processing server.
limitations: The comparison is line-oriented, not semantic. Reordered blocks, equivalent formatting, word-level changes, and very large documents may require a specialized diff tool.
sensitiveData: Suitable for local text, subject to your device and browser security.
notes: Treat moved lines as delete/add output and review context manually.

dataHandling: Conversion calculations happen in your browser. Entered values are not sent to an Anvil processing server.
limitations: Only the listed units are supported, and display rounding may not suit engineering, laboratory, financial, or regulated work. Confirm required precision separately.
sensitiveData: Suitable; numeric inputs are processed locally.
notes: Use authoritative factors and tolerances for regulated decisions.

dataHandling: Timestamp conversion happens in your browser and is not sent to an Anvil processing server.
limitations: Seconds and milliseconds can be confused. Local output depends on the device time zone, and historical or future daylight-saving rules may differ by platform.
sensitiveData: Suitable; timestamp values are processed locally.
notes: Confirm units and use UTC when exchanging system timestamps.

dataHandling: Encoding and decoding happen in your browser. Input text is not sent to an Anvil processing server.
limitations: Encoding a component is different from encoding a whole URL. Form encoding can treat plus signs differently, and decoding does not make an untrusted destination safe.
sensitiveData: Suitable for local text, but do not paste live secrets into examples.
notes: Inspect the final destination and query semantics before use.

lab.title: URL encoding in an HTML email fixture

dataHandling: Reference strings are selected in your browser. No entered data is uploaded to an Anvil processing server.
limitations: A copied string does not emulate a device, change browser behavior, or prove crawler identity. Fixed samples can become dated as browsers change.
sensitiveData: Suitable; use only in systems you own or are authorized to test.
notes: Do not use samples to evade access controls or impersonate verified crawlers.

dataHandling: UUIDs are generated in your browser and are not sent to or stored by an Anvil processing server.
limitations: UUIDs are identifiers, not passwords, access tokens, or proof of uniqueness across every possible system. Randomness depends on supported browser cryptography.
sensitiveData: Suitable for generating non-secret identifiers locally.
notes: Do not use a UUID alone as authentication or authorization.

dataHandling: Text is counted in your browser and is not sent to an Anvil processing server.
limitations: Counts use documented whitespace and JavaScript string rules rather than language-aware words or user-perceived grapheme clusters. Destination platforms may count differently.
sensitiveData: Suitable for local text, subject to your device and browser security.
notes: Use the destination platform's rules when a limit is strict.
